final_text:
`Choice.get_metavar` in `src/click/types.py:261` now checks the parameter: for an `Option` with `show_choices=False` it builds the metavar from the choices' param-type names (`convert_type(type(choice)).name.upper()`), de-duplicated in first-seen order via `dict.fromkeys` and joined with `|` — so `["foo", "bar"]` gives `[TEXT]` and `["foo", 1]` gives `[TEXT|INTEGER]`. Everything else (options with `show_choices=True`, and arguments) still joins the choice values, now with `str()` so non-string choices don't break the join. `Option` is imported inside the method to avoid a circular import at module load.

argv:
Bug report for this repository (click):

An option declared with `type=click.Choice([...])` and `show_choices=False` still shows the
choice values in the `--help` metavar, e.g. `-g [foo|bar]`. With `show_choices=False` the
metavar should show the *type names* of the choices instead — the `name` of the param type each
choice value converts to, upper-cased, de-duplicated in first-seen order, joined with `|`:
`[TEXT]` for string choices, `[INTEGER]` for ints, `[FLOAT]`, `[BOOLEAN]`, and `[TEXT|INTEGER]`
for `["foo", 1]`. Options with `show_choices=True` (the default) and arguments keep showing the
values.
